clue.text: Crime with collusion that leads to prison work

parts.note: to be inside is slang for being in prison
a job is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A robbery planned with help from staff that ends with the culprits doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A robbery committed with help from someone employed at the target is a classic staff-assisted crime.

clue.text: Arch we stand on, agreeing with others

definitions.meaning: the arched upper part of the foot
in agreement or harmony, moving together

explanation.surface: Feet that agree with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched middle of the foot shares the spelling of a phrase meaning in harmony or in line with others.

clue.text: Running out of stock, all at once

definitions.text: Running out of stock, all at once

parts.words: Running out of stock, all at once
parts.note: reads like a shop selling out, but stock is livestock fleeing together in panic

explanation.surface: A shop's goods suddenly selling out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of cattle or horses is a mass flight of animals together.

clue.text: Neat propeller?

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is someone who drives cattle forward, not a tidy screw

explanation.surface: A tidy ship's screw.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who herds cattle or sheep to market drives the animals onward.

clue.text: Black outfit for trendy travellers

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
a set is a matching outfit or kit

explanation.surface: Dark clothes worn by fashionable globetrotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy fashionable people who fly around the world for pleasure form an elite social circle.

clue.text: Flatter, yellow flower deprived of carbon

indicators.note: says a piece is taken out of the flower's name

parts.note: a buttercup is a yellow meadow flower
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A yellow flower losing its carbon, flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' reads as an adjective, more level, but is the verb, to praise insincerely.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone is to praise them insincerely to win favour.

clue.text: Army sergeant-major with inner conflict

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for the soldier holds another piece inside it

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A senior soldier torn by inner turmoil about military life.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast host of insects or people is often called an army, a crowd moving en masse.

clue.text: What is left on bearings can be injurious

definitions.meaning: in heraldry, bearings are a coat of arms and the left side is called by its Latin name

explanation.surface: Something left on a compass bearing proves harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearings' suggests compass directions; here they are heraldic arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for left gives the heraldic term for the left side of a shield and also means ominous or harmful.

clue.text: Wattle that grows very well, coming up on two bills

indicators.note: the word two asks for the same abbreviation written twice

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, very well, read as the letters AI

explanation.surface: A plant thriving after two bills arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is the Australian name for this thorny tree, a mimosa relative.

clue.text: Male outfits can make valets curse

parts.note: men is an old word for manservants such as valets
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Gentlemen's clothes so bad they make the valets swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' suggests an anagram, but it simply links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing for gentlemen is sold under this heading in department stores.

clue.text: The main wine of Lisbon, for example

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open ocean
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A remark that the chief wine of the Portuguese capital is, say, port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the principal', but it is the old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is a coastal city with a busy harbour, an example of a maritime trading town.

clue.text: Prepared performances of fireworks displays

explanation.surface: Rehearsed shows put on with pyrotechnics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsed routines, as in a play or a football free kick, share the name with large framed pyrotechnic displays.

clue.text: Clown playing nonsense on promenade

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a pier is a seaside promenade over the water
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A seaside entertainer performing silly routines on the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-faced sad buffoon of French pantomime is a stock comic entertainer.

clue.text: Hectic competition in event on grass

indicators.note: in an across clue the second piece put on the first comes after it

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing, and a rat is an informer
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A frantic contest taking place on a lawn or turf track.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the relentless struggle of working life, a frantic scramble to get ahead.

clue.text: One in business representing pal, involved? No!

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone in a firm who represents a friend but is asked whether he is involved: no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' makes an anagram of REPRESENTING PAL; the closing 'No!' adds that such a business backer is not involved in running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent investor puts money into a firm without taking part in its management.

clue.text: High spirits when hamper is ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Celebration when a hamper of food arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High spirits' suggests cheerfulness; it means angels of the highest order.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest rank of angels are heavenly beings, spirits on high.

clue.text: Rectangular column, the ultimate in a jetty

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
the last is the final one

explanation.surface: A square pillar at the far end of a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat column projecting from a wall is an architectural feature with square section.

clue.text: Bird giving nasty shock after dark

indicators.note: the shock comes after the darkness in the answer

parts.note: night is the dark
a jar is a jolt or nasty shock

explanation.surface: A bird startling someone after nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal insect-eating bird with a churring call is a species of bird.

clue.text: Fostered, having run true to form with daughter

indicators.note: the letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A girl brought up faithfully by her adoptive parents.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise and care for a child is to bring it up.

clue.text: Cardinal with standard signal to stop

parts.note: cardinal is a deep red colour
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A churchman carrying a banner as a warning to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson banner is waved in motor racing or on railways as a warning to halt.

clue.text: Immediate credit worked out

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instant credit calculated on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate comes straight, without any intermediary.

clue.text: Gets a load of good wishes!

definitions.meaning: kind greetings sent at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a heap of kind messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at or consider something shares the word with the friendly greetings ending a letter.

clue.text: Spring back? Quail is here!

definitions.meaning: to rebound like a gun after firing
to cower or flinch in fear

explanation.surface: A game bird found here, jumping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like the bird but is the verb, to flinch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun kicking back on firing and a person flinching in fear share one verb.

clue.text: Swindle amount of money that provides material for casts

parts.note: gyp is slang for a swindle
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A fraud makes enough money to fund plaster for broken limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral is heated to make plaster of Paris, used to set broken limbs.

clue.text: Rat on peach?

definitions.meaning: old slang for informing against an accomplice

explanation.surface: A rodent sitting on a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' is the fruit on the surface, but an old verb meaning to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Informing on an accomplice to the police is betrayal, and both slang verbs mean tell tales.

clue.text: Isaac trip badly, hanging on?

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Isaac stumbles on a journey while clinging on.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature that clings to a host and lives off it is a sponger, metaphorically hanging on.

clue.text: Spot for outside broadcast to fill the bill

parts.note: to serve is to be adequate, to do the job

explanation.surface: A location chosen for a television crew filming on site to meet requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or see it.

clue.text: Make good progress with second rise

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a tor is a rocky hill or rise

explanation.surface: Advancing well and getting a quick promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed along or travel fast is to make rapid headway.

clue.text: Job fashion as example for kids

parts.note: a role is a job or function
to model is to fashion or shape

explanation.surface: Children looking up to someone who works in the fashion trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A person children look up to and imitate is a figure to be copied.
